name: FeatureBench
description: An agentic coding benchmark evaluating end-to-end feature-oriented software development across 3,825 executable environments. Unlike SWE-bench (which tests single bug fixes), FeatureBench requires implementing new features spanning multiple commits and pull requests. Claude 4.5 Opus achieving 74.4% on SWE-bench drops to only 11.0% on FeatureBench — demonstrating that feature development is fundamentally harder than bug fixing.
evaluation_method: task success rate (automated test suite execution across entire repository)
reputation: Featured in 2025 AI conference proceedings; exposes the gap between bug-fixing and feature development capability; 3,825 executable environments is a large-scale evaluation; reveals significant limitations in agentic coding systems
notes: Feature development requires understanding existing code architecture, extending it coherently, and ensuring backwards compatibility across multiple files — significantly harder than isolated bug patches. Tasks are traced from unit tests along dependency graphs to identify cross-cutting feature work. The gap between SWE-bench (74%) and FeatureBench (11%) performance for the same model reveals that current agents are narrow bug-fixers rather than general software engineers.
